subject: Quality Assurance & Testing
title: ENIAC Wiring Errors
description: A micro-lesson that makes ENIAC Wiring Errors usable.

hook.text: ENIAC had 18,000 vacuum tubes. When one blew, operators searched for hours to find which one. Painful debugging.

buildup.text: The first computers were programmed by physically rewiring cables. A wrong connection was a literal 'bug.'

discovery.text: Debugging meant tracing wires by hand. There were no screens, no logs—just blinking lights and voltmeters.

twist.text: ENIAC's six female programmers invented debugging workflows. Their contributions were uncredited for decades.

climax.text: Those early debugging methods—isolate, reproduce, trace—remain the core process we use today.

punchline.text: Debugging started with pliers and wire. The logic hasn't changed.
